fields.v: Success criterion stated by the authors: per-task success on visible + hidden deterministic tests (official SWE-bench Docker evaluator for the hard slice); no success-rate threshold for a configuration. Cost criterion stated by the authors for prompt variants: 'wasteful' when median reasoning ratio > 1.5 with CI lower bound > 1.1, no material success gain, on multiple tasks (p. 13). (1) PI.DEV 0.82.1 + six Together-served open models (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi-K2.6, Kimi-K2.7-Code, Nemotron-3-Ultra, Inkling, GLM-5.2), holdout: multiple approaches 2.4-7.4x reasoning, confirmed wasteful on 6/6 (aggregate success 95.2% vs 96.5% baseline over 225 paired blocks); deep thinking 1.6-2.2x wasteful where selected; bounded efficiency neutral on 6/6 (GLM-5.2 0.48x). Quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost does not work for branching/deep-thinking/certainty variants (wasteful by the authors' rule), works for bounded efficiency (confirmed neutral). (2) Claude Code 2.1.220 via LiteLLM gateway + the same open models: ~100% pilot success, 5-30x cost per success vs PI.DEV, 10-41 turns vs 5-7. Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. (3) PI.DEV + Kimi-K3: 72/72 success; multiple approaches 16.6x, deep thinking 14.8x vs own (low) baseline; bounded efficiency 0.89x. Quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost as in (1). (4) PI.DEV + claude-sonnet-5 and native Claude Code + claude-sonnet-5 (162 runs, all valid): multiple approaches 2.70x / 2.52x output tokens; max certainty 4.13x output and 2.7x no-cache CPS under native Claude Code; native Claude Code baseline CPS ~15x PI.DEV. Quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors; cost does not work for these variants. (5) Adaptive-compute campaign, Sonnet 5 and Opus 5, 8 tasks: all solved at low effort; static max effort 1.5-2.8x CPS with no success gain; bounded efficiency caused 3/5 hidden-test failures on the ambiguous task. Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. (6) Claude Code 2.1.220 + Claude Opus 5, SWE hard slice: resolved 17/18/16 of 25 at low/high/xhigh, CPS $0.75/$1.89/$3.62. (7) Claude Code 2.1.220 + Claude Sonnet 5: 12/19/17 of 25, CPS $1.76/$2.32/$3.00 (high vs low p=0.016; xhigh vs low n.s. after Holm). Verdicts (6)-(7): no criterion stated by the authors. (8) DeepSeek Harness 0.1.0rc7 + Sonnet 5, 5 tasks x 3 reps: baseline $0.2753/run, policy -23.2%, rewrite -23.4%, effort -74.7%, full -82.2%, all 15/15 success (Claude Code activation benchmark: effort -19%, full -27%). Verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors

fields.v: Paired within task-model-harness blocks; prompt variants alter only the user instruction (objective, acceptance criteria and test command verbatim, validated automatically); frozen fixtures with hidden tests absent from the workspace; per-model top variants selected on development data and re-run on an 8-task frozen holdout (5 reps, n=40 per cell). Baseline: precise baseline prompt; own-harness baseline for controller arms; low effort for effort campaigns. Held constant: task, model, harness, nominal effort within a block; for dsh, model, tasks, prompts, evaluators and controller logic fixed while only the harness changes. Repetitions: up to 5 per cell; second repetitions on SWE discordant pairs. Statistics: task-clustered bootstrap CIs, sign-flip permutation, McNemar, Holm. Preregistered hypotheses H1-H8, H12-H17 frozen in the repository; extensions frozen before results. Human intervention: none

fields.v: Prompt content, not length, drives work: multiple approaches 2.4-7.4x reasoning (holdout-confirmed, no success benefit: 96.5% vs 95.2%, discordant 26:13 favouring baseline; easy cells 98.8% -> 96.4%, p~.003); deep thinking 1.6-2.2x; certainty 1.3-1.9x with redundant re-verification; verbatim repetition ~1x; bounded efficiency neutral-or-better. Redundant verification level 3+ costs 18x clean-run median. Harness gap larger: Claude Code 12-15x larger prefix, 2-7x more turns, 5-30x cost per success vs PI.DEV at comparable success; prompt effects do not transfer across harnesses. Effort: on hard SWE tasks Sonnet 5 benefits from high effort (7 rescues, 0 regressions), Opus 5 does not (low on the frontier); xhigh dominated. Harness x effort interaction: effort control saves ~75% under dsh vs ~19% under Claude Code. Caching cuts ~61% of the bill without changing behaviour

fields.v: Distinguished prompt variants, harnesses and effort levels on cost at high success; holdout and paraphrase/repetition analyses confirmed direction stability (one feature failed holdout; hard-cell branching signal failed cross-fitting). Limitations stated: high success ceilings limit detectable success effects to >= ~2.8 pp; adaptive-compute tasks produced no baseline failures; effort control did not reliably modulate computation on the Together-served open models; gateway can silently drop tool schemas or reasoning items; trace claims rely on visible reasoning and an imperfect judge; Claude Code arms smaller by design

fields.v: Replication package: https://github.com/PointFiveLabs/prompt-efficiency-benchmark (fixtures, hidden evaluators, prompts, runners, telemetry, analysis code). Pre-registration claimed: hypotheses, metrics and thresholds frozen in the repository before results (repository commits, not an independent registry); some extensions are post-registration; SWE-effort budget cap amended from $250 to $300 before outcomes were evaluated. Programming languages: Python, JavaScript, Go (core tasks); SWE-bench Verified (Python). Same authors as 'Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction'. Text says 'six open-weight models' in the core design but 'seven models with provider-exposed reasoning text' / 'all seven open-weight models' (Kimi-K3 added post-registration). Claude Code test-call share given as 'approximately half' (Sec. 6), 53-56% (Fig. 2) and ~52% (App. D). The Claude Code activation benchmark with the same controller (effort -19%, full -27%) is cited but its design is not reported in this paper. Absolute per-run costs small; multiplicative effects not extrapolated
